prompt: A photograph in a tight 4:3 frame, shot handheld and physically close at the shoulder of a pale young man, of a 22-year-old man lying on his back on a worn padded bench press in a cheap, low-ceilinged English leisure-centre gym, gripping a loaded barbell above his chest with both hands. He is pale, spotty, underfed, with a thin neck and uneven patchy stubble, wearing a faded grey supermarket-uniform hoodie with the sleeves pushed up and bright new protein-brand shorts, his thin white forearms trembling slightly, his face tilted back and looking straight up with a wide, trusting, slightly open-mouthed expression. Standing over him at the head of the bench, a tired man of about fifty leans down with both hands hovering just under the bar, spotting him, his weight on his back foot, a bit stooped, grey stubble, a sun-damaged creased neck, a heavy-lidded patient gaze fixed on the young man, wearing a faded cotton charity-fun-run T-shirt gone thin at the collar. Both faces are clearly visible, the young man's from below and the older man's from above, upside-down relative to each other, with real skin, visible pores, razor bumps, redness around the nose, under-eye shadows and no flattering polish. The light comes from flickering fluorescent strip lights on the low ceiling, giving flat greenish-white overhead light with hard shadows under the brows and chins, plus a little cool daylight from a grimy high window on one side. Around them: scuffed black rubber flooring, a cracked vinyl bench with a strip of gaffer tape on it, rust-speckled weight plates in uneven stacks, a dented dumbbell rack, a smeared mirror, a bare breeze-block wall painted a tired cream, all slightly out of focus behind them. Shot on a 35mm lens at eye level beside the bench, slightly low and close, with shallow depth of field, a subtle disposable-film grain and a muted palette of dull blues, institutional greens and tired yellows. Nothing has gone wrong yet; the mood is quiet and ordinary, with no readable text or logos anywhere. Thanks.
